fields.name: Fade
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3306BF0 (esv::TimelineSystem, Toolkit ProcessDeferredEndRequests) creates the component (bg3.exe+0x3313FD0: empty string, capacity 15) on the timeline entity of each deferred end request and assigns 'request string + "_" + text of the FixedString at request +0x18'. bg3.exe+0x2D10600 / 0x2D10A20 copy it into the screen-fade request and the player fade-in event.

fields.name: Duration
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3306BF0 copies the dword at request +0x1C; bg3.exe+0x2D10600 reads it as float: copied to the screen-fade-to request (+0x1C), and the maximum + 1.0 becomes the timeout of esv::timeline::FadedInUsersComponent.

fields.name: Users
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3306BF0 copies the set from request +0x20 (bg3.exe+0x5DF700); bg3.exe+0x2D10600 and 0x2D10A20 walk its key array (+0x40, count at +0x4C) with stride 4, one screen-fade request / fade-in event per element, stored as the user id.

fields.name: field_50
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3306BF0 copies the dword at request +0x50; bg3.exe+0x2D10A20 passes it on to esv::timeline::PlayerFadeInEventOneFrameComponent+0x20.

open_questions: field_50: probably the dialog instance id (live values 1..0x11C, passed on to esv::timeline::PlayerFadeInEventOneFrameComponent+0x20 and to the GameplayEventSystem callback), not proven.
The producer of the deferred end requests (system map with keys at +0x6B8 and 0x58-byte values at +0x6C8) was not found.
second_pass: All offsets and widths come from Windows code (bg3.exe+0x3306BF0, 0x2D10600, 0x2D10A20) and agree with 24 live instances (long STDString at +0, float 6.0/-1.0 at +0x18, HashSet<UserId> with one key at +0x20, small ints at +0x50). STDString is a builtin of generate.py now (24 bytes), so the earlier external_types override was removed.
